findings.claim: `_score_missing` scores incumbents and challengers against two different pctrank pools, so the two numbers the swap gate subtracts are not on the same scale — the exact thing the scale-compatibility contract in `us.py:score_names` forbids, despite the docstring claiming to honor it.
findings.evidence: kuroshio/cli.py:250 calls `profile.score_names(panel, tickers=[holdings])` (pool = holdings only) while kuroshio/cli.py:256 calls `profile.screen(panel)` (pool = every gate-passing column of the panel = holdings + candidates). Same panel, same session, one ticker: with close=[1101→100.0, 1102→100.1, 1103→100.2], `score_names(panel, ['1101','1102'])` gives 1102=1.0, and `screen(panel)` gives 1102=0.5. `_score_missing`'s docstring at kuroshio/cli.py:242-245 asserts "that split is the scale-compatibility contract"; the contract at kuroshio/core/screening/us.py:203-209 says the two must "stay comparable on the same scale", which requires the same cross-section, not just the same formula.
findings.repro: scratchpad/r4.py → prints `incumbent pool score_names([1101,1102]): {'1102': 1.0, '1101': 0.0}` vs `challenger pool screen(panel): {'1103': 1.0, '1102': 0.5, '1101': 0.0}`
findings.acceptance: Incumbent and challenger scores are produced from one cross-section (e.g. score the whole panel once with gate=False for ranking and use the gate only to decide challenger eligibility), plus a test asserting that a ticker present in both roles gets the identical final score from the same panel.
findings.route_reason: Spec names the scale-compatibility contract explicitly; violating it makes the printed score gap on a SWAP card a fabricated number.

findings.claim: Auto-filled incumbent scores are pctranked over the user's own holdings only, so the weakest incumbent is always exactly 0.0 (and a lone holding is 0.0 regardless of how strong it is), collapsing `turnover.hurdle` and making `propose` emit confidently wrong SWAP cards where it previously emitted an honest ALERT.
findings.evidence: kuroshio/cli.py:250 + kuroshio/core/screening/score.py:pctrank (`n<=1 → 0.0`; n=2 → {0.0,1.0}). Concrete: a sole holding 1103 whose close ramps 50→200 (the strongest name in the panel, unscored) scores 0.000, and a candidate 1101 whose close ramps 120→60 with a hand-typed `final_score: 0.20` wins: `SWAP 1103 → 1101 … gap of 0.200, above your IPS turnover hurdle of 0.150`. Second case: three names 0.1% apart (100.0/100.1/100.2) yield `SWAP 1101 → 1103 … a gap of 1.000`. Before this PR the same score-less holdings.yml produced the allocator's ALERT at kuroshio/core/allocator/engine.py ("No current holding has a screener score … run the screener before evaluating swaps") — a refusal, not a fabricated number. The PR's own acceptance test (tests/test_cli.py:`test_propose_scores_score_less_holdings_via_provider`) is an instance of this: 2 holdings ⇒ weakest is 0.0 by construction ⇒ the 0.90 candidate clears the hurdle no matter what the factor math says.
findings.repro: scratchpad/r3.py (sole-holding case) and scratchpad/r2.py (three near-identical names → gap 1.000)
findings.acceptance: Either the incumbent cross-section is widened to a real universe, or `propose` refuses to auto-fill below a minimum pool size and falls back to the existing ALERT; a test with a 2-name and a 1-name score-less holdings.yml pins that no SWAP is emitted on a fabricated gap. Deferring this to T26 is not acceptable: T26 says the hurdle gets "weaker for small portfolios" but the shipped behavior is wrong output on the acceptance case itself.
findings.route_reason: Dishonest published number: propose emits a SWAP card with a gap the data does not support, and regresses a case that previously produced an honest ALERT. Also lands on T4's own acceptance case.

findings.claim: The challenger side has the mirror-image bug not covered by the T26 debt note: when only one candidate clears Stage-1, `pctrank` returns 0.0 for it, so a genuine breakout is scored 0.000 and silently never proposed.
findings.evidence: kuroshio/cli.py:256 `profile.screen(panel)` on a panel containing only the user's own names; kuroshio/core/screening/score.py pctrank returns [0.0] for n==1. Holdings 1101 (120→60) and 1102 (140→70) both fail Stage-1, candidate 1103 ramps 50→200 with 5x volume — the only gate passer — and gets final_score 0.000, gap 0.000 < hurdle. Output: `No proposals — portfolio is within policy.` tasks/TODO.md T26 describes only the incumbent side and would not catch this.
findings.repro: scratchpad/r3.py, first block: prints `No proposals — portfolio is within policy.` for a monster-breakout challenger against two downtrending incumbents
findings.acceptance: A single gate-passing challenger receives a score that reflects its strength relative to a real cross-section (see R1's shared-pool fix), with a test pinning that a lone strong challenger against weak incumbents produces a SWAP.
findings.route_reason: Same root cause as R1; silently suppresses a valid proposal, so the 'produces scored cards end-to-end' acceptance is only accidentally met.

findings.claim: Relaxing `item["final_score"]` to `item.get("final_score")` turns a typo'd key into silence — candidates.yml has no unknown-key validation (unlike holdings.yml, which T3 deliberately made loud), so `final_scores: 0.90` is silently discarded, a network fetch is triggered, and a fabricated score replaces the user's intent.
findings.evidence: kuroshio/cli.py:75 (`item.get("final_score")`) with no `known`-key check anywhere in `_candidates_from_yaml` (kuroshio/cli.py:65-77), contrast `_holdings_from_yaml` kuroshio/cli.py:44-48 which raises `unknown key {key!r}`. Input `- {ticker: "1102", final_scores: 0.90, verdict: buy}` parses to `Candidate(final_score=None)`, fetches, and produces `Challenger 1102 scores 1.000 … gap of 0.600`. Pre-PR the same file raised `KeyError: 'final_score'`. No test covers a typo'd or unknown candidates.yml key.
findings.acceptance: `_candidates_from_yaml` rejects unknown keys with the same `path: ticker: unknown key 'x'` message `_holdings_from_yaml` uses, plus a test asserting exit 2 and the key name in stderr for `final_scores:`.
findings.route_reason: Regression introduced by this PR (loud KeyError -> silent drop), and the silently discarded value is then replaced by a fabricated score, so 'hand-written scores still win' fails on a typo.

findings.claim: Candidates rejected by Stage-1 are dropped with no message at all, so a user who lists 10 unscored candidates and gets "No proposals — portfolio is within policy" cannot tell whether the names were considered and lost or never scored.
findings.evidence: kuroshio/cli.py:259-260 `challengers = [c for c in challengers if c.final_score is not None]` — no stderr note, no count. With holdings `1101 score:0.4` and candidates `- {ticker: "1103", verdict: buy}` (downtrend) the run prints only `No proposals — portfolio is within policy.` The new test at tests/test_cli.py:`test_propose_scores_candidates_through_the_gated_screener` asserts `"1103" not in out`, i.e. it pins the silence as intended behavior. This is also a change in kind: previously every listed candidate carried a hand-typed score and was always evaluated.
findings.acceptance: Names dropped by the gate are reported (e.g. `notice: 1 candidate(s) had no hand-typed score and did not pass the Stage-1 gate: 1103`), with a test asserting the ticker appears in the notice.
findings.route_reason: 'No proposals - portfolio is within policy' is a claim this PR makes false: names were never scored, not evaluated and rejected.

findings.claim: README and ARCHITECTURE claim propose fills a missing score "with the same screener `screen` uses", which is false for every market (different pctrank cross-section) and additionally false for `us` (the 0.20-weight `sector` factor is silently dropped).
findings.evidence: README.md:53-54 "`propose` scores that holding with the same screener `screen` uses"; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:202-205 "filled from the screener (incumbents via `score_names`, challengers via the gated `screen`…)". The implementer's own tasks/TODO.md T25 states "an auto-filled score is not the same number `kuroshio screen --sector-map ...` would print for the same name on the same day", and R1 shows the number differs even without sector_map. Neither doc mentions that the pool is the user's own names, nor (in README) that `propose` now performs a network fetch.
findings.repro: Read README.md:53-54 against tasks/TODO.md T25/T26 and scratchpad/r4.py output
findings.acceptance: The docs state plainly that an auto-filled score is a percentile within the names in your own files (not a `kuroshio screen` number), and that `propose` fetches from the provider when any score is missing — or the code is changed to actually match the current wording.
findings.route_reason: README and ARCHITECTURE are documents of record; they now state something the code does not do.

findings.claim: Two behaviors this PR adds have no test that could go red: the `--provider` override and the `--market us` benchmark auto-append; every new test uses `--market tw` and a stub whose `get_provider` lambda ignores the provider name.
findings.evidence: kuroshio/cli.py:449 adds `--provider`, kuroshio/cli.py:288 resolves it, kuroshio/cli.py:293-294 appends `profile.benchmark`. tests/test_cli.py `_use_stub` is `monkeypatch.setattr("kuroshio.providers.get_provider", lambda name: stub)` — `name` is discarded, so deleting `args.provider or` would still pass. `profile.benchmark` is `None` for tw (kuroshio/core/screening/__init__.py PROFILES), so lines 293-294 are never executed by any new test; the only fetch-args assertion is `set(stub.calls[0][0]) == {"1101","1102","1103"}` on the tw path. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:202 now advertises `[--provider ...]` on propose.
findings.repro: pytest tests/test_cli.py -q after stubbing out `args.provider or` in kuroshio/cli.py:288 → still 121 passed
findings.acceptance: One test asserting `get_provider` is called with the value of `--provider` (stub captures `name`), and one `--market us` test asserting `SPY` is in the fetched ticker list.
findings.route_reason: MEDIUM but blocks nothing: no acceptance criterion violated, gate green, no dishonest claim. Coverage gap on two new flags -> T27.

findings.claim: `Candidate.final_score` is annotated `float` but now legitimately holds `None` between parsing and `_score_missing`; `propose()` sorts challengers by `final_score` and would raise `TypeError` if a `None` ever reached it.
findings.evidence: kuroshio/types.py:29 `final_score: float`; kuroshio/cli.py:75 now stores `item.get("final_score")` (None); kuroshio/core/allocator/engine.py `sorted(challengers, key=lambda c: c.final_score, reverse=True)`. Not reachable through `cmd_propose` today (the `any(... is None)` guard at kuroshio/cli.py:287 always routes to `_score_missing`, which filters), but `_candidates_from_yaml` is exercised directly in tests/test_cli.py and is now a documented-optional-field parser with a lying type.
findings.repro: python -c "from kuroshio.cli import _candidates_from_yaml; print(_candidates_from_yaml(p)[0])" on a candidates.yml with no `final_score:` → `final_score=None`
findings.acceptance: `final_score: float | None` on the dataclass, or `_candidates_from_yaml` returns only scored candidates.
findings.route_reason: LOW - scope boundary requires HIGH/MEDIUM to block. -> T28.

findings.claim: The new `--provider` flag has no `choices=` and an unknown value produces an uncaught `ValueError` traceback rather than exit 2 with a hint.
findings.evidence: kuroshio/cli.py:449 `p_propose.add_argument("--provider")`; kuroshio/cli.py:296 `get_provider(provider_name)` inside `try: … except ImportError`, while kuroshio/providers/__init__.py:23 raises `ValueError(f"Unknown provider {name!r}…")`. Same pattern already exists in `cmd_screen`/`cmd_backtest`, so this is a pre-existing shape reproduced on a new surface.
findings.repro: python -c "from kuroshio.cli import main; main(['propose','--ips','examples/ips-balanced.md','--holdings',h,'--market','tw','--provider','bogus'])" → `ValueError: Unknown provider 'bogus'` traceback
findings.acceptance: `except (ImportError, ValueError)` (or `choices=sorted(_REGISTRY)`) so an unknown provider exits 2 with the message on stderr, in all three commands.
findings.route_reason: LOW, and a pre-existing shape reproduced on a new surface (screen/backtest have it too). -> T29.
